question.prompt: A box contains a collection of triangular and square tiles. There are \(25\) tiles in the box, containing \(84\) edges total. How many square tiles are there in the box?

solutions.explanation:
A triangle has \(3\) edges and a square has \(4\), so a square contributes exactly one more edge than a triangle. If all \(25\) tiles were triangles, there would be
\[
25\cdot3=75
\]
edges. Replacing a triangle with a square keeps the number of tiles unchanged and adds exactly one edge.

The actual total has \(84-75=9\) extra edges, so exactly \(9\) tiles must be squares. This leaves \(16\) triangles, and \(16\cdot3+9\cdot4=84\), as required. There are \(\boxed{9}\) square tiles, choice D.
solutions.title: Start with all triangles
